# Mohamed Talaye

> Mohamed Talaye is a technology executive who builds technology organisations and the platforms they run on. Today, he is shaping the technology foundation for Aker BP's AI-native ambition.

Mohamed Talaye is a technology executive based in Oslo who builds technology organisations and the platforms they run on. Today, he is shaping the technology foundation for Aker BP's AI-native ambition. He was previously Chief Technology Officer of Orange Business. He speaks and writes about platform strategy, AI-native operations, invisible OSS and sovereign cloud.

## Pages

- [Profile](https://mohamedtalaye.com/): who I am and what I work on
- [Speaking](https://mohamedtalaye.com/speaking.html): keynotes, panels and interviews
- [Writing](https://mohamedtalaye.com/writing/): articles
- [Bio](https://mohamedtalaye.com/bio.html): official bios, photos and talk descriptions

## Writing

- [Invisible OSS: From Operational Support to AI-Native Network Intelligence](https://mohamedtalaye.com/writing/invisible-oss.html): Invisible OSS does not mean OSS disappears. It means the complexity of operations disappears from the customer experience, because intelligence, automation and control move inside the network.
- [From CTO to Chief Visionary Officer: How AI May Redefine Technology Leadership](https://mohamedtalaye.com/writing/cto-to-chief-visionary-officer.html): As AI agents take on more of architecture, development and execution, technology leadership may shift from supervising delivery to shaping vision, structured intent and trust. A personal reflection on the AIshore era.
- [B2B Connectivity in the AI Era: The Future Is Not Just More Bandwidth](https://mohamedtalaye.com/writing/b2b-connectivity-ai-era.html): AI changes the nature of enterprise traffic, not only its volume. The future of B2B connectivity is connectivity plus intelligence, plus control, plus trust, delivered as a platform.
- [AI and blast radius: change the control system, not the scope](https://mohamedtalaye.com/writing/ai-and-blast-radius.html): A response to Philippe Ensarguet on AI-written code in mission-critical systems. The risk is not AI generating code. The risk is AI generating code without fast, intelligent feedback loops.
